source.author: Go course authors (drafted by an AI model)

source.provenance: Drafted by an AI model for the course ladder in contemporary Bokmål (2005 norm); not reviewed by a native speaker. It is controlled, deliberately repetitive Norwegian written for learners and may contain unnatural phrasing. Facts about Norway and Bergen are general knowledge and unchecked. The English lines are the drafter's own.

review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting native-speaker review. House style: moderate Bokmål with three genders (ei/-a for feminine nouns, en/-en masculine, et/-et neuter), weak past in -et, neuter definite plural in -ene, sju and tjue, "ble", "ga". Anna receives a job offer in Oslo and must choose. A realistic everyday dilemma told in the past tense with dialogue; no real hospital is named.

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: En dag fikk Anna et brev. Det var et tilbud om ny jobb på et sykehus i Oslo.
sentences.english: One day Anna got a letter. It was an offer of a new job at a hospital in Oslo.

sentences.text: Anna leste brevet to ganger. Hun var glad, men hun var også redd.
sentences.english: Anna read the letter twice. She was happy, but she was also afraid.

sentences.text: Hun hadde jobbet på klinikken i mange år. Hun likte jobben, og hun likte pasientene.
sentences.english: She had worked at the clinic for many years. She liked the job, and she liked the patients.

sentences.text: Men sykehuset i Oslo var stort, og de trengte en sykepleier som henne.
sentences.english: But the hospital in Oslo was big, and they needed a nurse like her.

sentences.text: Hvis hun sa ja, måtte hun flytte fra Bergen.
sentences.english: If she said yes, she would have to move away from Bergen.

sentences.text: Jeg har fått et tilbud, Lars. Jeg vet ikke hva jeg skal gjøre.
sentences.english: I have received an offer, Lars. I do not know what to do.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Et tilbud om jobb? Hvor?
sentences.english: An offer of a job? Where?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: På et sykehus i Oslo. Sjefen skrev til meg. Han vil at jeg skal komme.
sentences.english: At a hospital in Oslo. The boss wrote to me. He wants me to come.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Det er et godt tilbud. Men du bor her, og du har jobb her.
sentences.english: It is a good offer. But you live here, and you have a job here.
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Vil du flytte, Anna?
sentences.english: Do you want to move, Anna?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Jeg vet ikke. Jeg vil ikke flytte fra dere. Men jeg vil også lære mer.
sentences.english: I do not know. I do not want to move away from you. But I also want to learn more.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Det er et vanskelig valg. Du må tenke lenge.
sentences.english: It is a difficult choice. You must think for a long time.
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Anna gikk til Marta. Marta hørte på henne.
sentences.english: Anna went to Marta. Marta listened to her.

sentences.text: Hva sier hjertet ditt?
sentences.english: What does your heart say?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Hjertet sier at jeg er glad her. Men jeg lurer på om jeg kan gjøre mer.
sentences.english: My heart says that I am happy here. But I wonder whether I can do more.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Du kan be om hjelp. Gud hjelper deg, og vi hjelper deg også.
sentences.english: You can ask for help. God helps you, and we help you too.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Anna ba den kvelden. Hun ba om hjelp og om fred i hjertet.
sentences.english: Anna prayed that evening. She prayed for help and for peace in her heart.

sentences.text: Neste dag skrev hun til sjefen. Hun takket for tilbudet, men sa nei.
sentences.english: The next day she wrote to the boss. She thanked him for the offer, but said no.

sentences.text: «Jeg vil lære mer,» skrev hun, «men jeg vil bo her et år til. Kanskje kommer jeg senere.»
sentences.english: "I want to learn more," she wrote, "but I want to live here one more year. Maybe I will come later."

sentences.text: Lars og Sam var glade. Marta sa: «Du har bestemt deg. Det er bra.»
sentences.english: Lars and Sam were glad. Marta said: "You have decided. That is good."

sentences.text: Utsikten fra toget var bra. Etter tunnelen var det lyst igjen. Sam kom tilbake fra Oslo, og han gikk ut på stasjonen.
sentences.english: The view from the train was good. After the tunnel it was light again. Sam came back from Oslo, and he went out onto the station.

sentences.text: Sam har fortsatt tvil. Han er ikke sikker på alt, men han kjenner Gud og er trygg. Han venter på svar.
sentences.english: Sam still has doubt. He is not sure of everything, but he knows God and feels safe. He waits for an answer.

sentences.text: Folk skriver bokmål eller nynorsk, og ordene er forskjellige. Hvorfor? Det er to måter, og ingen er feil. Dialektene er også forskjellige.
sentences.english: People write Bokmål or Nynorsk, and the words are different. Why? There are two ways, and neither is wrong. The dialects are also different.

sentences.text: Mel, salt og gjær blir deig. Deigen må hvile før ovnen. Brødet lukter godt, og det smaker bra.
sentences.english: Flour, salt and yeast become dough. The dough must rest before the oven. The bread smells good, and it tastes good.

sentences.text: Først bygger de skolen, og så åpner de den. Sam går dit, og der er det plass.
sentences.english: First they build the school, and then they open it. Sam goes there, and there is room there.

sentences.text: Langt fra stasjonen kjøpte Sam billett. En dame gikk ut av toget før ham.
sentences.english: Far from the station Sam bought a ticket. A woman got off the train before him.
